name: Andris Kulbergs
role: Prime Minister of the Republic of Latvia (Ministru prezidents)
party: Apvienotais saraksts (AS, United List: Latvian Green Party, Latvian Regional Alliance, Liepāja Party), elected on its list as a non-party member — the United List's MEP sits with the European Conservatives and Reformists (ECR)
bio: Andris Kulbergs, born in 1979, is a Latvian businessman from the car trade who has been Prime Minister of Latvia since 28 May 2026. A graduate in international business of Concordia International University in Tallinn, he worked for the telecoms operator Lattelecom and then ran car-dealing companies, including the Latvian arm of the Inchcape group, and led the car dealers' association Auto Asociācija. Elected to the 14th Saeima in 2022 on the United List ticket without joining any of its parties, he chaired parliamentary inquiries into the cost overruns of the Rail Baltica railway and into Riga's district-heating prices. After Evika Siliņa (New Unity) resigned on 14 May 2026, President Edgars Rinkēvičs asked him to form a government, and his four-party coalition of the United List, the National Alliance, New Unity and the Union of Greens and Farmers was approved by 66 votes to 25 with security, budget stabilisation, safe elections and the fight against cartels and corruption as its priorities; in office he has dealt above all with the restructuring of the state-owned airline airBaltic, which filed for Chapter 11 protection in a US court in September 2026, with cutting Rail Baltica's costs and with support for Ukraine. At the Saeima election of 3 October 2026 the United List won 35.3% of the vote and 41 of the 100 seats, the most for any list in Latvia's parliamentary history, and as of 23 October 2026 he remains Prime Minister with his cabinet in office while he negotiates a new coalition, the President having named him on 6 October to form the next government once the new Saeima convenes on 3 November.
